## 1. The actual halted alphabet, not an abstract drain
Use precisely the unified generator (SHA c083a0d491e7eb44ee0e575d222ba256152c56a682cadedd08d7785c6032105f): reset-first C phases, complete irreversible commitment, complete terminal/abort/ready and A/Q refresh channels, actual finite-rate monitors, fast cleanup, all newly added A_i→Q0 resets including A_k, and later acquisition at the already fixed positive zeta. Set only the first A0↔A1 edge amplitude to zero.

Write R_h for the declared full raw-read/write resource footprint. Define

    P_h = 1_(clock A0) product_(r in R_h) 1_(tag_r not o_h,z_h),
    B_h = I-P_h.

These B_h are NONREADY flags, not the history flags used in the memory energy. Workspace and monitors are unrestricted. The entire halted Hamiltonian commutes each P_h:

* Later acquisition, C gates, Q verification, and their reversals have no A0-ready endpoint.
* A0 consistency-abort or cleanup sources have an own o_h/z_h tag and hence lie in B_h. Cleanup interchanges o_h and z_h, preserving their union.
* R abort phases remain busy, and coherent cleanup is forbidden in every R phase by the reset-first amendment.
* All monitor Hamiltonians preserve clock/tag labels.
* Other owners can change only their own labels and free labels, never create/remove h's o_h/z_h predicate. They cannot change h's clock.

Resolved resets are also noncreating. Acquisition/commit/terminal/abort sources are nonready; Q_k→A0 may become ready but cannot start in P_h. A/Q refresh preserves the coarse clock/tag predicate. The z_h→free reset can remove the last orphan h tag but cannot create one. Other-owner resets and monitor channels preserve P_h. Complete bundled losses commute P_h. Thus, including coherent malformed masks, not only basis populations,

    L_0^* B_h = -A_exit,h,    0 <= A_exit,h <= nu B_h,       (1)

with a volume- and epsilon-independent local nu. This follows directly from the resolved source/target blocks and [H,P_h]=0; it does not interpret Hamiltonian paths as trajectories. Consequently P_h is an absorbing physical subspace and

    0 <= exp(u L_0^*)B_h <= B_h.                            (2)

## 4. Full-state correlated-noise readiness hierarchy
If necessary center every local HP perturbation adjoint by

    N_Z^0(O)=N_Z(O)-{N_Z(I),O}/2.

The aggregate is unchanged because sum_Z N_Z(I)=0; each new summand is local, HP, identity-annihilating and has cb norm at most twice the old one. No individual summand is assumed Lindbladian. Bath-only identity-annihilating terms act trivially on the system-only tests.

Choose a buffered separated owner set U whose witness supports are disjoint and no nominal term touches two supports. For M_U=product_(h in U) Z_h, exact locality gives

    L_0^*M_U <= -r |U| M_U.

A joint system/bath perturbation touching K subset U satisfies

    N_Z^*M_U <= ||N_Z^*||cb M_(U\K).

Indeed untouched system factors factor out; the touched product has norm at most one; HP plus the cb norm bounds its image above by that norm times the joint identity. Untouched factors commute the whole touched map even with a shared arbitrary bath. A body-q perturbation touches at most a fixed q_eff disjoint witness supports, and their fixed size gives incident budget C eta per witness. This does not require a fixed noise-partner graph.

Writing x_U=Tr(rho M_U), induction in |U| and scalar comparison with

    p'=-rp+C eta p^(1-q_eff),       p(0)=1,
    p(u)^q_eff=exp(-q_eff r u)+(C eta/r)(1-exp(-q_eff r u))

gives x_U<=p(u)^|U| when eta is small enough that p<=1. Using (4),

    Tr rho(u) product_(h in U) B_h <= [p(u)/alpha]^|U|.    (5)

This is on the FULL physical CPTP evolution, from any initial joint state. A packing constant P_pack gives, for arbitrary S, a separated U subset S with |U|>=|S|/P_pack. Once b=p(T)/alpha<1,

    Pr(all h in S nonready) <= b^(|S|/P_pack).

If there are at most c_H N owners, a union bound over m=ceil(beta N) subsets yields

    Pr(sum_h B_h >= beta N)
       <= binom(c_H N,m) b^(m/P_pack) <= exp(-a_beta N)   (6)

for sufficiently small fixed b. Choose T to make its exponential-decay term small, then eta to make its floor small. Both choices are independent of epsilon. Initial readiness, actual reset records, mask dephasing, and independence are unnecessary.

## 5. Uniform relative-F cost of switching off initiation
This is the main new analytic interface. Let W=V G be the accepted global exponential/activity weight and F=T(W), T=T_B T_t. All notation here is in the exact forest frame; first acquisition has identity DATA gauge, so its removal has the same bounded local support there.

For a unit-amplitude first-edge adjoint commutator D_h, define the LINEAR map

    R_h=T^{-1} D_h T.

Fixed-depth cancellation leaves only a bounded causal cone. Its cb norm is uniformly bounded as epsilon tends to zero:

* Every dirty inverse is the actual fresh triangular inverse with fixed s_min>0. Its local norm and support do not depend on epsilon.
* Each useful factor is Id+t(Q_h-Id), with Q_h UCP and t=c epsilon^2. Its inverse has cb norm <=(1-2t)^(-1) for t<1/2. Thus the unweighted isolated resolvent pole never appears in this estimate.
* The number and size of gates in a local cone are fixed. Activity gates and their inverses are uniformly bounded for delta=d epsilon^2 in a fixed small interval.

Conjugate R_h through Y in G=Y^dagger Y. Disjoint gates cancel, leaving a bounded-support HP map of bounded norm. Split raw V=exp(sE) into unaffected commuting factors and the bounded affected-energy factor. The latter lies between fixed positive scalars, independent of N and epsilon. The usual direct local relative estimate, valid also for the resulting NONUNITAL map, gives

    +/- R_h(W) <= C W.

Only NOW apply the positive map T. This yields

    +/- D_h F <= C F.                                  (7)

No inequality is pushed through T^{-1}; its only role is exact algebra and a finite local norm bound. In fact this argument works for any fixed local HP perturbation, but only the removed Hamiltonian edges are needed. Summing their physical coefficients epsilon gives

uniformly for sufficiently small epsilon. The same bound holds throughout a finite ramp scaling those amplitudes between epsilon and zero, with unchanged resets and supports.
